scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC3 (10.3.0.100) in Office B reports it cannot reach anything outside its own
subnet -- no Internet, no Office A, no Server Room -- though it can still reach
other hosts on its own VLAN. Other Office B hosts are unaffected. PC3 was working
before a desktop reconfiguration. Diagnose.

injection.action: point PC3's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 10.3.0.99

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc3 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: PC3's correct gateway is 10.3.0.1 (its VLAN SVI/VRRP VIP). It was
  reconfigured to 10.3.0.99, which is inside PC3's subnet but is not assigned to
  any device, so ARP for the gateway never resolves and PC3 cannot forward any
  off-subnet traffic. Same-subnet hosts remain reachable (direct ARP), which is
  why intra-VLAN traffic still works.
Localization: pc3
Root cause: PC3's default gateway set to 10.3.0.99 instead of 10.3.0.1
Fix: restore PC3's default route -- `ip route add default via 10.3.0.1`
scenario.fix_spec: restore PC3's default route -- `ip route add default via 10.3.0.1`

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: PC3’s local IP stack (host routing/default gateway configuration).
- Mechanism: PC3 has a wrong default gateway. Its routing table shows “default via 10.3.0.99 dev eth0,” so any traffic to destinations outside 10.3.0.0/24 is sent to 10.3.0.99. ARP for that next hop fails (“incomplete”), so the kernel returns “Destination Host Unreachable.” In-subnet traffic still works because it is delivered directly at Layer 2.
- Localization: PC3 (10.3.0.100) on eth0. Evidence: ip route on PC3 shows default via 10.3.0.99; ip neigh/arp shows 10.3.0.99 incomplete; ping to 10.3.0.99 fails with host unreachable; ping to 10.3.0.1 (expected gateway on Office B VLAN) and to 10.3.0.2 (DSWB1 subinterface) succeeds.
- Root cause: During the desktop reconfiguration, PC3’s default gateway was set to the non-existent 10.3.0.99 instead of the correct gateway (10.3.0.1 on VLAN B2).
- Corrective fix: On PC3, replace the default route with the correct next hop or re-enable DHCP to obtain the proper gateway:
  • ip route del default; ip route add default via 10.3.0.1 dev eth0
  • Make the change persistent in the OS network config (netplan/NetworkManager/etc.), then flush ARP (ip neigh flush all) or simply retry.
After correction, PC3 should reach Office A, Server Room, and the Internet. No issues were found on distribution/core; other Office B hosts already use the correct gateway (10.3.0.1).

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies PC3 as the affected device and describes a host-side default-gateway misconfiguration.
The report explicitly identifies PC3's default gateway/default route (default via 10.3.0.99) as the affected component and explains its misconfiguration.
Explicitly replaces PC3's incorrect default route with the correct gateway (ip route add default via 10.3.0.1) and makes it persistent, which matches the expected fix.

Logs show PC3 has 10.3.0.100/24, ARP for 10.3.0.99 is incomplete and pings to .99 fail while pings to .1 and .2 succeed; the writeup's conclusion (wrong default gateway on PC3 pointing at a non-existent .99) follows logically. Minor gaps: the explicit 'ip route' default line and evidence that other hosts use .1 are not fully displayed in the log, but the core observations support the diagnosis and fix.
